**(Section)**

There is no disagreement that he (ﷺ) was born in the heart of Makkah, and that his birth occurred in the Year of the Elephant. The affair of the Elephant was a foreshadowing (*irhas*, a preparatory sign before prophethood) that Allah sent ahead for His Prophet and His House. The people of the Elephant were Christians, People of the Book, and their religion at that time was better than the religion of the people of Makkah, who were worshippers of idols. Yet Allah granted victory over the People of the Book to those who were idolaters, a victory in which humans had no part. It was a foreshadowing and a preparation for the Prophet (ﷺ) who would emerge from Makkah, and a magnification of the Sacred House.

**(Benefit)**

When the Prophet (ﷺ) reached the valley of Muhassir (a valley between Mina and Muzdalifah, belonging to neither), he urged his she-camel forward and hastened his pace. This was his custom at places where the punishment of Allah had descended upon His enemies. There, the People of the Elephant were struck by what Allah has related to us. For this reason that valley was called the Valley of Muhassir, because the Elephant was exhausted (*husira*) there, that is, it was wearied and unable to continue on to Makkah. He acted in the same way when passing through al-Hijr, the dwellings of Thamud: he covered himself with his garment and hastened his pace.

Muhassir is a barrier between Mina and Muzdalifah, belonging to neither of them. Uranah is a barrier between Arafah and al-Mash'ar al-Haram (the sacred landmark), and there is a barrier between every two sacred sites that belongs to neither of them.

Mina is part of the sacred precinct (*haram*) and is a sacred site (*mash'ar*). Muhassir is part of the sacred precinct but is not a sacred site. Muzdalifah is both a sacred precinct and a sacred site. Uranah is not a sacred site and is outside the sacred precinct (*hill*, the permitted area). Arafah is outside the sacred precinct (*hill*) and is a sacred site.

**(Section)**

Consider his (ﷺ) saying: «Indeed Allah withheld the Elephant from Makkah, and gave power over it to His Messenger and the believers.»

How is it understood from this that the subjugation of the inhabitants of Makkah by His Messenger and his victorious army is greater than the subjugation by the Elephant, which would have entered it against them by force? He withheld the Elephant from them and gave power over them to His Messenger and the believers, until they conquered it by force after subjugation, the authority of force, and the humbling of disbelief and its people. That was of greater rank, of greater significance, a more manifest sign, a more complete victory, and a higher word. It was far above admitting them under the bondage of a truce, the dictates and conditions of the enemy, and withholding from them the authority, might, and triumph of conquest by force, in the greatest conquest He granted to His Messenger, by which He strengthened His religion and made it a sign to the worlds.

**(Benefit)**

Reflect on the wisdom in the placement of the vulva of the female animal: it was placed at the rear so that the male can mount her for mating. Had it been placed at the underside of her belly, as it is in women, the male could not mate with her except in the position in which a woman has intercourse.

It is mentioned in the books on animals that the vulva of the female elephant is on the underside of her belly. When mating time comes, it rises, protrudes and emerges for the male, so that he can mate with her.

Thus, since in the elephant it was made contrary to what is found in the rest of the animals, it was singled out for this distinctive feature, so that the matter by which offspring continues would be facilitated.

**(Section)**

Then reflect on the trunk of the elephant and the wondrous wisdoms in it. It serves in place of a hand for taking fodder and water and bringing them to its stomach. Were it not for this, it could not take anything from the ground, since it has no neck to extend as the rest of the cattle do. When the neck was absent, a long trunk was substituted in its place to fill its role. It was made able to lower it, raise it, bend it and manipulate it however it wishes. It was made a hollow, soft-surfaced receptacle, so with it the elephant takes what it needs, carries what it wants to its stomach, holds within it what it desires, uses it as it wills, gives, and takes when it wishes.

Ask the one who denies the Creator (*al-mu'attil*): who provided it with this in place of the neck?

And who substituted for the organ that was withheld something that stands in its place and takes its role, other than the Compassionate, the Merciful toward His creation, who ensures their welfare, the Gentle toward them?

And how could this come about in the absence of design, with the world devoid of its Sustainer, its Originator, its Creator and its Fashioner? There is no god but Him, the Mighty, the Wise.

If you say: why was it not created with a neck like the rest of the cattle, and what is the wisdom in that?

It is said, and Allah knows best His wisdom in His creation: because its head and its ears are a tremendous and great matter and a heavy load. Had it had a neck like other necks, its neck would have been broken by its weight and weakened by carrying it. So its head was placed close to its body, so that no part of its weight and burden would fall upon it. In place of the neck He created this long trunk, with which it takes its nourishment. And since the camel's neck was lengthened for this wisdom, its head was made small in proportion to the greatness of its body, so that its weight would not harm it and weaken its neck.

Glory be to Him whose wisdoms exceed the count of those who count and the enumeration of those who enumerate.
